arxiv-2411-00978.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Julien Barrat, Enrico Marchetto, Alessio Miscioscia, Elli Pomoni. arxiv-2512-05298.title: A Conservative Discontinuous Galerkin Algorithm for Particle Kinetics on Smooth Manifolds Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
arxiv-2512-05298.creator: Grant Johnson, Ammar Hakim, James Juno
arxiv-2512-05298.description: Abstract A novel, conservative discontinuous Galerkin algorithm is presented for particle kinetics on manifolds. The motion of particles on the manifold is represented using using both canonical and non-canonical Hamiltonian formulations. Our schemes apply to either formulations, but the canonical formulation results in a particularly efficient scheme that also conserves particle density and energy exactly.

pmc-10605847.description: Simple SummaryChemotherapy is one of the most widely used cancer treatments. A significant barrier to its successful use is the high risk of acquiring the phenomenon of multidrug resistance in cancer. In this regard, today, researchers’ attention is focused on solving this critically important problem.

pmc-11452624.title: Effects of iron supplements and iron-containing micronutrient powders on the gut microbiome in Bangladeshi infants: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-11452624.creator: Andrew Baldi, Sabine Braat, Mohammed Imrul Hasan, Cavan Bennett, Marilou Barrios, Naomi Jones, Imadh Abdul Azeez, Stephen Wilcox, Pradip Kumar Roy, Mohammad Saiful Alam Bhuiyan, Ricardo Ataide, Danielle Clucas, Leila M. Larson, Jena Hamadani, Michael Zimmermann, Rory Bowden, Aaron Jex, Beverley-Ann
pmc-11452624.description: Anemia is highly prevalent globally, especially in young children in low-income countries, where it often overlaps with a high burden of diarrheal disease. Distribution of iron interventions (as supplements or iron-containing multiple micronutrient powders, MNPs) is a key anemia reduction strategy. Small studies in Africa indicate iron may reprofile the gut microbiome towards pathogenic species.

pmc-11534717.title: Discovering a novel glycosyltransferase gene CmUGT1 enhances main metabolites production of Cordyceps militaris
pmc-11534717.creator: Rong-an He, Chen Huang, Chun-hui Zheng, Jing Wang, Si-Wen Yuan, Bai-Xiong Chen, Kun Feng
pmc-11534717.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Cordyceps militaris is a filamentous fungus used for both medicinal and culinary purposes. It exhibits a wide range of pharmacological activities due to its valuable contents of cordycepin, polysaccharides, carotenoids, terpenoids and other metabolites. militaris strains are highly susceptible to irreversible degradation in agricultural production, which is often manifested as a prolonged color change period and a significant decrease in the production of secondary metabolites.

pmc-12815910.title: MCARE enhances SERCA1 activity in fast-twitch muscle to maintain calcium handling and muscle integrity
pmc-12815910.creator: Takashi Sasaki, Hayataka Takase, Michinori Koebis, Atsu Aiba, Yu Takahashi, Yoshio Yamauchi, Ryuichiro Sato
pmc-12815910.description: The release of Ca2+ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into the cytoplasm, followed by its reuptake by sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA), is critical for the muscle contraction-relaxation cycle. In this study, we identify a small transmembrane protein, predominantly expressed in fast-twitch muscles, which regulates SERCA1 activity.

pmc-13063873.title: Clinical evaluation of the efficacy and safety of nasturtium herb and horseradish root versus placebo in the continuous prophylaxis of recurrent uncomplicated cystitis: a double-blind randomised clinical trial
pmc-13063873.creator: Uwe Albrecht, Gregor Schmitz, Ulrich Stefenelli, Nina Kassner, Meinolf Wonnemann, Lukas Schablauer, Niklas Lonnemann, Lisa Felix, Ruth Kirschner-Hermanns
pmc-13063873.description: Background and objectivesThis study aimed to demonstrate the efficacy and safety of a herbal combination drug of nasturtium herb and horseradish root in the continuous prophylaxis of recurring uncomplicated cystitis.MethodsThe clinical trial was conducted as a phase III, two-armed, placebo-controlled, randomised, double-blind, prospective, and multi-center study, which followed a parallel-group design in Germany.

pmc-13147106.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026LB206 LB206 - SUBOPTIMAL LAA OPACIFICATION: A NOVEL FUNCTIONAL BIOMARKER OF STROKE RISK IN AF AND ESUS – RESULTS FROM PHASE-III DAYLIGHT TRIAL AND PHASE-IV BROAD DAYLIGHT STUDIES
pmc-13147106.creator: Luciano Sposato, Diana Ayan, Sebastian Fridman, Eduardo Soriano Navarro, Arturo Gonzalez Lara, Lakni Abeyesekera, Federico Liberman, Fawaz Alotaibi, Mobeen Ahmed, Rodrigo Bagur
pmc-13147106.description: Background and aimsStroke risk stratification in Atrial Fibrillation (AF) and Embolic Stroke of Undetermined Source (ESUS) relies on prognostic markers rather than on the immediate thrombus substrate. We aimed to test a new concept in stroke risk stratification: Suboptimal Left Atrial Appendage Opacification, or SLAAO (/ˈsleɪ.oʊ/). SLAAO is a newly defined imaging mechanistic biomarker reflecting LAA hypocontractility and stasis.

pmc-13240443.title: Omega‐3 DHA as a blank canvas: A molecular approximation to how lipid mediators modulate LGR6 in inflammation resolution
pmc-13240443.creator: Álex Pérez‐Sánchez, Mireia Garcia‐Viloca, Àngels González‐Lafont, José M Lluch
pmc-13240443.description: The leucine‐rich repeat‐containing G protein‐coupled receptor 6 (LGR6) has a potential role in inflammation resolution and different cancer processes. In this study, we employed computational techniques, including molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations of mammalian membrane‐embeded systems, to understand the activation mechanism of LGR6 upon binding of the specialized pro‐resolving lipid mediator maresin 1.

pmc-13542413.title: Micro/Nanoscale Acoustic Manipulation: From Particle Control to Autonomous Microswimmers
pmc-13542413.creator: Jiahui Chu, Lemin Zhang, Xu Wang, Wenzong Li, Yahua Liu
pmc-13542413.description: Acoustic manipulation and propulsion technologies have emerged as powerful platforms for micro/nanoscale control, enabled by their non‐contact operation, label‐free compatibility, biocompatibility, and strong penetration capability. This review systematically examines the physical mechanisms and recent advances in acoustically enabled passive particle manipulation and autonomous microswimmer propulsion.

pmc-13554638.title: Synergistic remediation: Integrated adsorption and degradation techniques for multiphase environmental decontamination
pmc-13554638.creator: Shama Hegde, Sriraksha Rao, Sowmya R Holla
pmc-13554638.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This review critically examines integrated adsorption–degradation strategies for the remediation of air, water, and soil contaminants, with emphasis on recent advances reported since 2020. Rather than treating adsorption and degradation as standalone processes, the review highlights how adsorption functions as an effective pretreatment step that enhances degradation efficiency by increasing the pollutant concentration at reactive interfaces, improving mass transfer, and stabilizing reactive species.

pmc-13569788.title: Sarcoidosis: A Clinical Trials Perspective
pmc-13569788.creator: Juan J Zapata-Huizi, Manuela Herrera-Tamayo, Josmar J Ríos-Poveda, Eli N Pérez-Rodas, Fernanda Hernández-González, Jacobo Sellares
pmc-13569788.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Sarcoidosis is a systemic granulomatous disorder of unclear origin, most commonly impacting the lungs and mediastinal lymph nodes. Respiratory manifestations occur in most patients and are the main contributors to disease-related morbidity and mortality. Despite decades of clinical experience, the evidence base for treatment has historically been limited, with corticosteroids serving as first-line therapy largely on the basis of observational data and expert consensus rather than robust randomized controlled trials.

pmc-13601642.title: The Stress of Being Left Out: Physiological and Behavioral Responses to Ostracism in Preverbal Infants
pmc-13601642.creator: Giada Basset, Ermanno Quadrelli, Chiara Turati, Hermann Bulf
pmc-13601642.description: Being ostracized is a stressful experience that affects behavioral and physiological reactivity in adults. However, evidence regarding its impact early in life remains limited. This study investigated whether inclusion or exclusion during a ball‐tossing game influenced physiological and behavioral reactivity in 8‐month‐old infants (N = 59; 24 girls and 35 boys).

pmc-13609556.title: Nasoalveolar Molding and Feeding in Infants with Cleft Lip and Palate: An Exploratory Study of Parents’ and Caregivers’ Perceived Experiences
pmc-13609556.creator: Enrique España-Guerrero, Esther Liceras-Liceras, Alba España-Guerrero, Adoración Martínez-Plaza, Ingrid Garzón, Ricardo Fernández-Valadés, Fernando Campos, Antonio España-López
pmc-13609556.description: Background/Objectives: Patients with cleft lip and palate (CLP) typically experience feeding difficulties due to an abnormal communication between the oral and nasal cavities, and novel therapies such as palate tissue engineering and nasoalveolar molding (NAM) are in need to improve the final outcomes.

uslaw-usc-t10-s1585a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s1585a.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 81 (Civilian Employees). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Authority.— The Secretary of Defense may authorize any DCIS special agent described in subsection (b)— (1) to execute and serve any warrant or other process issued under the authority of the United States; and (2) to make arrests without a warrant— (A).
